title: TscpPulseArtifact
description: Verifier output artifact. Produced by the TSCP reference emitter. Consumed by TscpAdapter. This schema is the trust boundary — both producer and consumer are bound to it. Do not modify without a version bump.

schema_version.description: Artifact schema identifier. Bumped only on breaking changes. Adapter must reject unknown versions.

artifact_id.description: UUIDv4. Unique per artifact emission. Not a commit SHA — identifies this specific output file.

created_at.description: UTC ISO 8601 timestamp. Real artifact creation time from the emitter. Must not be hardcoded, deterministic, or faked. A frozen timestamp creates 'reproducible but false' artifacts.

provenance.description: Full backward provenance chain. Given these five fields, an independent verifier can checkout the commit, rebuild, verify the binary matches, and recheck the proof.

manifest_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the frozen benchmark_manifest.json. The immutable anchor. References the environment under which this artifact was produced.

repo_commit.description: Full 40-char git SHA of tscp-anchor at artifact generation time. Must match manifest.commits.tscp_anchor.sha.

binary_digest.description: SHA-256 of the verifier/prover binary. A different binary digest means a different build environment — results are not directly comparable.

proof_digest.description: SHA-256 of the proof bytes. Must be stable across reruns for the same (commit, inputs). A changed proof_digest signals non-determinism or a prover change.

transcript_digest.description: SHA-256 of the Fiat-Shamir transcript bytes. Transcript stability is a separate invariant from proof stability.

status.description: Outcome of verify(). 'pass' = valid proof. 'fail' = invalid proof (constraint violation). 'error' = emitter-side exception.

verifier_unchanged.description: True iff the verification key and circuit are identical to the reference. A GPU speedup claim is only valid when this is true — the verifier must be the same on both sides of the comparison.

correctness_gate_passed.description: True iff status=pass AND proof_digest is stable AND transcript_digest is stable. If false, any performance numbers in this artifact are invalid and must not be cited.

fiat_shamir_rounds.description: Number of Fiat-Shamir challenge rounds. Must be stable for the same circuit. Drift here indicates a protocol change.

public_inputs_hash.description: SHA-256 of the public inputs. Ensures the verified statement is what was intended.

benchmark.description: Benchmark measurements. Two distinct sub-objects: integrity (prove+verify, not for speedup claims) and performance (prove only, use for speedup claims).

layer.description: Which benchmark layer this artifact covers. One artifact = one layer. Do not conflate. kernel=AVX-512 butterfly etc; primitive_integration=sumcheck/FRI/transcript; end_to_end=full pipeline.

trace_size.description: NTT trace size. Should be a power of two. E.g. 256, 1024, 4096, 16384, 65536.

integrity.description: Integrity benchmark: prove() + verify() + digest check, all timed. Answers: is the prover correct and what does the full pipeline cost? Do NOT use for speedup claims — verification cost is included.

proving_ms.description: prove() wall time within the integrity run.

verification_ms.description: verify() wall time. Counted inside integrity.

total_pipeline_ms.description: prove + verify + gate. The end-to-end correctness-verified cost.

performance.description: Performance benchmark: prove() ONLY in the timed region. verify() runs outside the timed region but must pass before results are accepted. USE THIS for CPU→GPU speedup claims, not integrity numbers.

proving_ms.description: Timed region: prove() only. This is the number for speedup ratio calculations.

fri_ms.description: null if FRI is not applicable for this layer.

verification_outside_timed_region.description: Must be true. Verification ran outside the timed region and passed. A performance artifact without this being true is invalid and must be rejected by the adapter.

statistics.description: Aggregate statistics across repetitions. Populated when repetitions > 1.
